Right Triangle Calculator

Complete a right triangle from two known measurements, such as two legs or a leg and an acute angle. The answer includes both acute angles and the hypotenuse, using degrees for angle inputs. The acute angles sum to 90°. Side ratios follow sine, cosine, and tangent; with legs a,b, hypotenuse c=√(a²+b²). In the side-angle mode, the given leg is treated as opposite the entered angle; the second leg and hypotenuse are derived from the trigonometric ratios.

How to use this calculator

  1. Enter known measurements, leg a, leg b or angle.
  2. Select Calculate to see the answer and its breakdown.
  3. Keep a scenario, change an input and compare the results.

Use consistent units and check the assumptions below before applying the result.

How right triangle is calculated

The acute angles sum to 90°. Side ratios follow sine, cosine, and tangent; with legs a,b, hypotenuse c=√(a²+b²). In the side-angle mode, the given leg is treated as opposite the entered angle; the second leg and hypotenuse are derived from the trigonometric ratios. A 3-4-5 right triangle has acute angles about 36.87° and 53.13°.

a²+b²=c²; sin(θ)=opposite/hypotenuse; acute angles sum to 90°.
A worked example

A 3-4-5 right triangle has acute angles about 36.87° and 53.13°.

Assumptions & useful context

The result depends on the values you enter and the method described above. Displayed numbers may be rounded; calculations use the unrounded values. Check that this model matches your situation before relying on it.

Frequently asked questions

Can both entered angles be acute angles?

This tool accepts one acute angle plus a side or two sides, not two redundant angles.

What if I enter a side and its opposite angle?

Select the supported side-angle mode and ensure the angle is between 0° and 90°.
